analysis:
Examined the memory-admission changes in ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift and the one-line wiring in ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift. The PR adds releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad() (ModelLoading ~1323-1326), which releases retained free KV segments via GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and then clears the MLX cache via clearCacheAfterConfirmedNativeOwnership(). It is called from evictUntilAvailable (once before the first eviction, and in the no-candidate self-heal path) and from fastAdmissionReject. The StartupPreloader gets a new reclaimBeforeSkip dependency (StartupPreload line 244-245). reclaimableMemoryBytes now also counts CBv2RetainedKVSegments.retainedBytes.

Security relevance: these are availability and memory-accounting changes only. No new input from the coordinator or consumers, no change to key handling, attestation, encryption, or routing. Releasing free KV segments and the MLX buffer pool is conventional; the pool memory is overwritten on reuse. It is consistent with T-028 (residual GPU data) and arguably marginally better for it. It does not touch the prefix-cache storage tier (T-041), TTL, HMAC naming or the KEK. Eviction safety checks (in-flight, local reservation, MTP retention, autopilot pins) are unchanged, since unloadModel(forEviction:) remains the authoritative gate. A possible availability concern is that releasing retained KV segments while busy engines run could cause extra reallocation, but that is a performance question rather than a security regression. The implementation of GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments, busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory, and the StartupPreloader reclaimBeforeSkip semantics are outside the supplied evidence (StartupPreloader.swift is not shown), so I could not confirm that a concurrent release cannot disturb live KV grants. The base-side StartupPreload text shows no issue. No findings.
